result.stdout:
efrpg - EntityFramework Reverse POCO Generator tool

Usage:
  efrpg --database <type> --connection <string> [--timeout <seconds>] [--stored-procedures]

Options:
  --database, -d        Database type: SqlServer, PostgreSQL, MySql, SQLite, Oracle
  --secrets-stdin       Read connection strings as XML from stdin. Preferred: unlike the options below,
                        the value never appears in process listings or command-line audit logs.
                        Format: <Secrets><Connection>..</Connection><MultiContextConnection>..</MultiContextConnection></Secrets>
  --connection, -c      Connection string. Convenient for interactive use, but VISIBLE IN PROCESS LISTINGS.
  --connection-base64   As --connection, UTF-8 base64 encoded to sidestep shell quoting. Base64 is not
                        encryption - this is equally visible in process listings.
  --timeout, -t         Command timeout in seconds (default: 600)
  --stored-procedures, -sp  Read stored procedures, table-valued and scalar-valued functions (slow on large databases)
  --synonyms            Include database synonyms when reading tables, foreign keys, and stored procedures
  --enums-base64        Enum specs (XML, UTF-8 base64). When set, the tool reads only enum rows. Used by the T4 template.
  --multi-context       Also read multi-database-context settings from the MultiContext.* tables.
  --multi-context-connection-base64  Connection string for the multi-context settings database (UTF-8 base64).
  --version, -v         Print the tool version and the wire format schema version, then exit.
  --help, -h            Print this help.

Output: XML written to stdout. Errors written to stderr.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = startup error, 2 = partial failure (some reads failed).
